newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss investors plan new Geneva-based airline.
newsitem.headline: Swiss investors plan new Geneva-based airline.

text.p: A group of investors, including the Canton of Geneva, are considering founding a new airline -- Swiss World Airways (SWA) -- to fly between Geneva and the U.S.
Jean-Charles Simon, member of the Swiss parliament and SWA chairman, said the airline plans to start operating in the second half of 1997 with two leased Boeing 767 aircraft.
SWA is in response to a decision by Swissair, part of the SAirGroup, last year to scrap most of its loss-making long-haul flights from Geneva in favour of the Zurich hub.

"As an international city we cannot be satisfied by just having a regional airport. It must be part of a long-distance network and without going through Kloten (Zurich Airport)," Simon told daily newspaper Tages-Anzeiger.

Simon said SWA could be profitable if it was able to capture just half of the at least 320 passengers daily that he said Swissair had lost by cancelling almost all its long-distance flights from Geneva.
The Boeing 767 aircraft would have 208 seats each.
Swissair's decision to focus its operations in Zurich were strongly criticised by both national and local politicians from the French-speaking part of Switzerland.

SAirGroup's chief executive Philippe Bruggisser has argued that neither Swissair, nor Switzerland can afford to have two international airports and unless Switzerland focuses on Zurich it might be without an international airport one day.

Asked about SWA, Bruggisser on Thursday told a news conference at Crossair AG, the regional airline in SAirGroup, that he takes any potential competitor seriously, but he also warned that potential losses on long-haul flights are large and the risks in such a project are large.
SWA already has a share capital of 300,000 Swiss francs and the canton of Geneva has contributed 60,000 of this.
The aim is to have a start capital of 50 million francs and Simon said he already had commitments for part of that.

Earlier this week Simon told Swiss News Agency (SDA) that municipalities in the French-speaking part of Switzerland, Swiss and multinational companies, and investors from the Middle East had expressed interest in the project.
Among the cities that SWA could serve from Geneva are New York, Washington, Boston, Chicago or Canada's Montreal.
